findings.reason: a done-when that passes on the unfixed code measures nothing, and every case must be rebuilt around the shape the new condition can actually change: a run that still holds a live pointer while its ledger row records the promotion.
findings.text: §102's done-when measures a state the derivation never produces: the obligations view builds every promotion duty from classifier rows that come only from live pointers (`_classified_rows` → `_live_pointers` → `runs.list_live`, `reckon/crew/obligations.py:636-638`), and promotion unlinks that pointer as it writes the ledger row (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:1162-1163`), so for a run whose pointer is gone, as in the plan's first and third cases, no `review-ready`, `promotable-stale` or `promotable` row is produced on the unfixed code either — both cases pass without the change, and the declared controls ("removing the ledger condition fails the first case", "dropping promotion duties on the pointer's absence alone fails the third") exercise no failing state.

findings.reason: as written the section sends a node to add a condition on a path that already yields the wanted outcome, and to leave untouched the settlement where a stale `review-ready` would survive a re-derivation.
findings.text: §102 nominates the wrong code path for its own evidence: the Why says the pointer "was gone and its ledger row was written" yet the duty persisted, but the full derivation it now targets produces no duty at all for a run with no live pointer (`_obligations_view` iterates `_live_pointers` only, `reckon/crew/obligations.py:1753-1756` over `_classified_rows` at `:636-638`), and the one read-time settlement that can outlive the pointer, `without_departed_run_duties` (`reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1032-1062`), is explicitly declared unchanged and keeps `review-ready`; so either the evidence misdescribes the pointer state (the pointer was present when the row was derived and the row's 12 min 43 s is its age, not its persistence) or the fix lands on a path the symptom never takes.

findings.reason: the node cannot satisfy its own done-when inside its declared write paths, so it will either stop as a scope blocker or land a row that blocks the stop it promises not to.
findings.text: §103 says `repair-round` "joins `NON_BLOCKING_DUTY_KINDS` … so it is listed but never holds the coordinator's stop open", but the stop gate does not read that constant: the hook carries its own mirror, `_NON_BLOCKING_KINDS` (`reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:239-241`), and `_blocking_items` decides from that set alone (`:1304-1315`), because the hook cannot import the derivation; with write paths limited to `reckon/crew/obligations.py` and the new test, the row will be listed and will still block, contradicting the deliverable and failing the case "The stop-hook text lists it without blocking the stop".

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §102 builds its cases around a run whose live pointer is gone, a shape the obligations derivation never produces a duty for, so its negative controls cannot fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both units measure through a named test file under `tests/`, and neither directs evidence to a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `repair-round` names the mechanism, and the two test filenames describe what they assert; no plan labels or ticket numerals reach a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §102 places the condition on a derivation path that yields no duty for a run with no live pointer, so it cannot produce the listing its own evidence reports; §103 places the rule on a constant the stop gate does not read.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each unit names one deliverable: §102 removes one duty kind for a promoted run; §103 adds one duty kind for a repair round.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §103's `plan-section-depends-on` entry (`s103` → `s102`) resolves to an existing section and §102 needs no upstream; both write `reckon/crew/obligations.py` in sequence, so the ordering is coherent.
